questions.scenario: A new `@Service` in package `ng.itlearning.payments` isn't found at startup ('required a bean of type ... that could not be found'). The main class annotated @SpringBootApplication is in `ng.itlearning.bank.app`.
questions.question: What is the most likely cause?
options: The service needs @Autowired on the class
Component scanning starts from the main class's package and its sub-packages, so ng.itlearning.payments is never scanned
questions.explanation: Put the main class in the root package (e.g. ng.itlearning) so every feature package is beneath it, or configure scanning explicitly.

questions.scenario: In code review you see `@Autowired private AccountRepository repo;` on a service. The reviewer asks for a change.
questions.question: What is the preferred style and why?
options: Setter injection, because it is more flexible
Constructor injection with a final field: dependencies are explicit, the object is complete after construction, and unit tests can use plain new
Keep field injection but make it public
questions.explanation: Constructor injection is the Spring team's recommendation. Field injection hides dependencies and forces reflection or a Spring context in tests.

questions.scenario: A singleton `@Service` keeps `private BigDecimal dailyTotal` and adds each transfer's amount to it. Under load the totals are wrong.
questions.question: What's the root cause?
options: Singleton beans are shared by all request threads, so mutable instance state is a race condition
Spring creates a new service per request
questions.explanation: One instance serves every thread. Keep beans stateless; put shared state in the database, Redis or a thread-safe structure.

questions.scenario: Two beans implement `NotificationSender` (SMS and email). Startup fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException at AlertService's constructor.
questions.question: Which fixes are valid?
options: Mark one implementation @Primary, or use @Qualifier at the injection point, or inject List<NotificationSender> if all are needed
questions.explanation: Spring needs a way to choose: a default (@Primary), an explicit choice (@Qualifier), or a collection of all candidates.

questions.scenario: A team adds `spring-boot-starter-data-redis` for a cache in one feature. The next deploy fails health checks because the app tries to connect to Redis on localhost:6379.
questions.question: Why did this happen?
options: Auto-configuration is driven by the classpath: the starter's presence activated Redis auto-configuration with default connection properties
questions.explanation: @ConditionalOnClass conditions switch on when a library appears. Configure the connection properties for each environment (or exclude the auto-configuration if unused).

questions.scenario: You define your own `DataSource` @Bean with a custom HikariCP configuration. A colleague worries Spring Boot will create a second DataSource too.
questions.question: What actually happens?
options: The auto-configured DataSource is guarded by @ConditionalOnMissingBean, so it backs off and yours is used
Two DataSources are created and startup fails
questions.explanation: Auto-configuration is designed to step aside when you provide a bean of the same type. Prefer properties first, though: replacing the bean also replaces the defaults you got for free.

questions.scenario: You need to know why `DataSourceAutoConfiguration` did not apply in a test environment.
questions.question: What is the quickest way to find out?
options: Read every Spring Boot source file
Start the app with --debug (or check the actuator conditions endpoint) and read the conditions evaluation report's negative matches
questions.explanation: The report lists every auto-configuration and the exact condition that matched or failed, for example 'did not find required class' or 'found bean of type DataSource'.
